method: Two independent fact-checking passes over the same 56 answers, one per model. Each pass used four reviewers, one per task, each reading all 14 answers to that task. Reviewer prompts were byte-identical across passes; only the model varied. Reviewers were instructed to judge technical correctness only and explicitly not to penalize brevity, terseness, omitted detail, or informal tone.

opus.note: Same model that generated the answers.

sonnet.note: Different model from the generator. Run to test whether same-model review shares blind spots.

sonnetOnlyFinding.error: Offers useMemo alongside useRef to stabilize a WebSocket. useMemo is documented as a performance optimization with no cleanup hook; React may discard and recompute the value without closing the old socket, reintroducing the leak.
sonnetOnlyFinding.note: The one error the same-model pass missed. Confirms the shared-blind-spot concern is real but small at this sample size.

crossModel.interpretation: The two passes applied different error thresholds, and most of the gap is threshold rather than blindness. Opus flagged any factually wrong claim, including a wrong branch offered alongside a correct one ('it either hoists one version and gives it to both, or nests two copies' — the first branch never happens). Sonnet flagged sole-cause errors and self-contradictions and let hedged imprecision pass. The T3 split is the clean demonstration: Sonnet flagged exactly the two files that list 429 as retryable and then say 'never retry a 4xx' (self-contradictory) and cleared the four that say 'never retry a 4xx' without mentioning 429 (merely overbroad). Verified by grepping the files for 429. That is a consistent narrower criterion, not inconsistency. Eight of the thirteen Opus-only findings are explained this way. The remaining five fail even Sonnet's narrower criterion and are genuine misses: C-r1-T1, A-r2-T1, D-r2-T1, A-r1-T2, D-r2-T2. Neither pass dominates — Opus was broader, Sonnet found one error Opus was blind to. Treat the union, 36 of 56, as the working figure and still a floor.

filesWithErrors.error: Claims a resolver hoists one version and gives it to a package whose declared range excludes it. Resolvers nest a second copy instead.
Same hoisting misconception as A-r2-T1, stated as one of two branches.
Tells the reader to delete the lockfile after an overrides change. Changing package.json already invalidates the affected entries; deleting the lockfile re-resolves every unrelated dependency.
Attributes a stale tree to aggressive pnpm resolution caching. pnpm re-resolves on overrides change and errors under --frozen-lockfile.
Entire causal explanation rests on the hoisting misconception. Also claims adding a direct dependency changes how another package's dependency resolves.
Offers 'picks one and hopes for the best' as a resolver branch. That describes bundler-level dedupe, not package-manager resolution.
Given non-overlapping ranges, no package manager hands a ^1.2.0 dependent a v2 copy. Verified by reading the file: 'it either hoists one version to the top and gives it to both'.
Offers 'picks one version and breaks the other' as a branch; the resolver installs both.
'Indexes make writes slower, always.' False for a targeted UPDATE/DELETE on the indexed column, and for Postgres HOT updates touching no indexed column.
Claims a composite on (a, b) beats separate indexes on a and b. It only serves the leftmost prefix, so b-only lookups regress.
Lists 429 as retryable, then says never retry a 4xx. 429 is a 4xx.
Claims Square accepts an idempotency key header. Square takes idempotency_key as a request-body field.
Same Square header error; advises sending a header that Square would ignore.
'A 4xx means the server heard you and said no.' Tells the reader to give up on 429, the canonical retry-with-backoff signal.
Self-contradictory 429/4xx retry advice, plus the Square header error in its most explicit form.
'Do not retry on 4xx.' Overbroad; 429 and 408 are retryable.
'Never retry a 4xx, because the request was wrong and the next one will be wrong the same way.' Overbroad for 429 and 408.
Overbroad 4xx advice, plus a claim that retrying with the same idempotency key 'burns' it.
Offers useMemo alongside useRef to stabilize a WebSocket. useMemo has no cleanup hook and may recompute without closing the old socket.
Describes a self-amplifying listener loop that its own code sample contradicts: the shown effect has a stable [url] dep, so it does not re-run per render.

recurringErrorClasses.name: hoisting misconception (T1)
recurringErrorClasses.note: A package manager never resolves a dependency to a version outside a dependent's declared range; non-overlapping ranges produce a nested second copy. G-r1 is the only answer that correctly conditions the shared-copy outcome on the ranges overlapping. The Opus reviewer verified this empirically by installing conflicting packages; the Sonnet reviewer flagged it in one file and cleared it in five others.

recurringErrorClasses.name: never-retry-4xx (T3)
recurringErrorClasses.note: 429 is a 4xx and is the canonical retry-with-backoff response. Both D reps stated the qualified version correctly. Four of the six instances are in E/F, the variants instructed to cut phrases that do not change the meaning.
